Hi Samira — I’m Laura from Redwood Legal. I’ll expand on Karthik’s note with the legal specifics you asked about.

1) EU transfers (SCCs):
- Redwood relies on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module: Controller–Processor, where applicable) to provide an appropriate safeguard for transfers of personal data from the EEA to jurisdictions without an adequacy decision. Our DPA contains selectable clauses so the SCCs are incorporated by reference and executed as part of the DPA.
- We keep SCCs updated to the Commission’s latest text and will incorporate any required amendments.

2) UK transfers (IDTA / UK Addendum):
- For data originating in the UK, we offer the UK International Data Transfer Addendum (IDTA) / UK Addendum. We can either: (a) attach our standard UK Addendum to the DPA, or (b) incorporate the IDTA text if you prefer the standalone UK text. Either approach is commercially acceptable — please confirm which Acme prefers and we’ll prepare the DocuSign package accordingly.

3) Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA / DTIA):
- Redwood performs internal Transfer Impact Assessments for relevant processing flows. We can provide a redacted customer-facing TIA summary that covers: destination jurisdictions, legal landscape (e.g., US surveillance risks), our contractual safeguards (SCCs/UK Addendum), and the technical and organizational measures (TOMs) we apply at the infrastructure layer.
- We only provide a full, non-redacted TIA under a mutual NDA or as part of an enterprise security review (to protect internal security controls). If Acme needs deeper detail we can discuss an information-sharing agreement.

4) Subprocessors:
- The attached CSV is the current roster. We operate a notification cadence (per the DPA) and offer a “customer-specific” subprocessors notice for customers who require a signed attestation. For highly regulated customers we also support a limited subprocessor approval process during procurement.

5) Technical & contractual safeguards summary (high level):
- SCCs/UK Addendum + DPA contractual commitments.
- Encryption at-rest and in-transit; key management options for Private deployments; SOC 2 + internal audits.
- Data residency options for Dedicated/Private customers.

If you’d like, I can mark up your procurement team’s DPA redlines directly into our version and propose language for the UK Addendum attachment. Otherwise we can prepare our DPA + UK Addendum for signature and include a customer-facing TIA summary.

Let me know which path you prefer and any procurement deadlines.

Kind regards,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0246
